doc.title: David Friesen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 24, 2024

title: Titles, This Light Has No Darkness, favorite albums, and 'jazz is full of good manners'
summary: He keeps a list of titles, discusses the chamber orchestra album and favorite Rollins and Ornette records, the Seattle free scene, and his father's lesson about kindness.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: Okay. At what point do titles come to you and attach themselves to songs?

Yeah you know I have a sheet — a sheet on my iPhone under notes and it’s funny, the relationship there, a funny pun notes, it is notes, of different titles that come to me and I write them down. And then I’ll have a tune and it will fit this title. Sometimes the title and the music comes together at the same time, something I haven’t written down. So there’s — it’s different all the time. It’s different. Now “This Light Has No Darkness” this is the new album with the 33-piece chamber orchestra program. This is almost like here’s where my music has come to at this point. One or a few of my favorite albums are “Our Man in Jazz” Sonny Rollins on RCA Victor, “Our Man in Jazz” Henry Grimes, with Billy Higgins, Don Cherry and Sonny of course. The album called “Ornette,” Scott LaFaro is playing bass on that one, Billy Higgins again. Yeah Ornette’s music and Sonny Rollins. So those are some things I’m listening to a lot and you know I play concerts with Sam Rivers and I’ve played, I was part of the free music scene in Seattle in the ‘60s. So I played a lot of that music. “This Light Has No Darkness” doesn’t resemble that but it’s part of the path that brought me to this place of “This Light Has No Darkness” and of course “This Light Has No Darkness” it means just that. This particular light has no darkness or this light is the truth.

Without arguing about religion — because I won’t argue about religion. Everyone has a choice to make in their lives and the freedom to do what they would like to do. My dad told me something I’ve never forgotten, that I haven’t really lived up to in my life’s path you know I’m 82 years old now, so up to this point, but I’ve been stronger in the later years. My dad says, “everyone responds to kindness.” That’s a big one. You know? And as you know jazz is full of good manners, of allowing a person, if they’re playing a phrase [scats] you know they start this phrase and I’ll hear this and I might have heard something prior to that was going to move in that direction but when I hear this I have to put on the brakes and allow the Mack truck to go and then I can make the right hand turn so to speak. You know you have to be quick to allow individuals to hear what they want to hear and that’s where my response has to add to that music. A lot of times, most times by not getting in the way.
Well you just gave me a David Friesen quote, “jazz is full of good manners.”
